title: ESSAY 1: Financial Inclusion — India's Journey and the Road Ahead

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Financial inclusion guarantees affordable access to essential financial services, including savings, credit, insurance, and pensions for vulnerable groups.
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) acts as the foundational pillar for universal banking access across India.
The JAM (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) trinity enabled seamless Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT), significantly reducing leakages and corruption.
India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), led by UPI, drastically reduced transaction costs and expanded micro-payments in rural areas.
The next frontier of financial inclusion requires boosting financial literacy, deepening credit delivery to MSMEs, and facilitating gender-inclusive coverage.

blocks.content: Financial inclusion is not merely a social obligation, but a fundamental prerequisite for sustained and equitable economic growth.

items: PMJDY was launched on August 28, 2014, under the National Mission for Financial Inclusion.
RBI's Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index) tracks progress across three parameters: Access (35%), Usage (45%), and Quality (20%).
